pp:me:2014:q1-s4.question: Which one of the following equations is a correct identity for arbitrary 3x3 real matrices P, Q and R?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} (P+Q)^{2} &=P^{2}+P Q+Q P+Q^{2} \\ &=P \cdot P+P \cdot Q+Q \cdot P+Q \cdot Q \\ &=P^{2}+P Q+Q P+Q^{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:me:2014:q2-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 2
pp:me:2014:q2-s4.question: The value of the integral $\int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^{2}\sin(x-1)}{(x-1)^{2}+\cos(x-1)}dx$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:me:2014:q27-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 27
pp:me:2014:q27-s4.question: The value of the integral $\int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{x}e^{x+y}dydx$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$I=\int_{0}^{2}\left[\int_{0}^{x} e^{x+y} d y\right] d x$

$\int_{0}^{x} e^{x+y} d y=\left.e^{x+y} d y\right|_{0} ^{x}=e^{2 x}-e^{x}$

$\quad I=\int_{0}^{2}\left(e^{2 x}-e^{x}\right) d x$

$\quad I=\left.\frac{1}{2} e^{2 x}\right|_{0} ^{2}-\left.e^{x}\right|_{0} ^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left(e^{4}-1\right)-\left(e^{2}-1\right)$

$\quad I=\frac{1}{2} e^{4}-\frac{1}{2}-e^{2}+1$

$=\frac{1}{2} e^{4}-e^{2}+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left(e^{4}-2 e^{2}+1\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(e^{2}-1\right)^{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:me:2014:q30-s4.question: A shaft is subjected to pure torsional moment. The maximum shear stress developed in the shaft is 100 MPa. The yield and ultimate strengths of the shaft material in tension are 300 MPa and  450 MPa, respectively. The factor of safety using maximum distortion energy (von-Mises) theory  is  _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1}&=100 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{2}&=-100 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$ As per Von-Mises yield theory: $N^{2}\left[\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2}$ $\text{In this case, } \sigma_{3}=0$ $2 N^{2}\left[\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}-\sigma_{1} \sigma_{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2}$ $\Rightarrow N^{2}\left[(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}\right] \leq(300)^{2}$ $\Rightarrow N^{2}=\frac{9}{3} \Rightarrow N \leq \sqrt{3}$ $\therefore \quad N=1.732$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1.75** (acceptable range: [1.7, 1.8]).

pp:me:2014:q33-s4.question: It is desired to avoid interference in a pair of spur gears having a 20$^{\circ}$ pressure angle. With increase in pinion to gear speed ratio, the minimum number of teeth on the pinion

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Machine - Gear and Gear Train
detailed_solution.markdown:
For $20^{\circ}$ stub pressure angle spur gears pair minimum number of teeth on the pinion can be expressed as

$t_{min}=\frac{2A_p}{\sqrt{1+G(G+2)\sin ^2 \phi -1}}$

Where,

$A_p:$ Fractional addendum for one module in order to avoid interference.

$G:$ Gear ration

$\phi :$ Pressure angle

Now we have given that speed ratio is increased & we know that;

$\text{Speed ratio}=\frac{1}{\text{gear ratio}}$

So if gear ratio is increased we can say that minimum number of teeth on pinion must be increase to avoid interference.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2014:q34-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 34
pp:me:2014:q34-s4.question: A uniform slender rod (8 m length and 3 kg mass) rotates in a vertical plane about a horizontal axis 1 m from its end as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the angular acceleration (in rad/$s^{2}$) of the rod at the position shown is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} A P &=1 \mathrm{m} \\ A C &=4 \mathrm{m} \\ P C &=3 \mathrm{m} \\ I_{C} &=\frac{m L^{2}}{12}=\frac{3 \times 8 \times 8}{12} \\ &=16 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ I_{P} &=I_{C}+m(P C)^{2} \\ &=16+3 \times 3^{2}=43 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text { Torque } &=m_{2} g \times \frac{P B}{2}-m_{1} g \frac{A P}{2} \\ T &=m_{2} \times 9.81 \times \frac{7}{2}-m_{1} \times 9.81 \times \frac{1}{2}\\ &=34.335 \mathrm{m}_{2}-4.905 \mathrm{m}_{1} \\ m_{1} &=\frac{3}{8} \mathrm{kg}, \mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{3 \times 7}{8}=2.625 \\ T &=34.335 \times 2.625-4.905 \times 0.375 \\ &=88.29 \mathrm{N} \mathrm{m} \\ T &=I_{P} \alpha \\ \alpha &=\frac{T}{I_{p}}=\frac{88.29}{43}=2.053 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2** (acceptable range: [1.9, 2.1]).

pp:me:2014:q35-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 35
pp:me:2014:q35-s4.question: A bolt of major diameter 12 mm is required to clamp two steel plates. Cross sectional area of the threaded portion of the bolt is 84.3 $mm^{2}$. The length of the threaded portion in grip is 30 mm, while the length of the unthreaded portion in grip is 8 mm. Young's modulus of material is 200 GPa. The effective stiffness (in MN/m) of the bolt in the clamped zone is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Machine Design - Bolted, Riveted and Welded Joint
detailed_solution.markdown:
$k_{t}=\frac{A_{4} E}{4}$ (Stiffness in threaded portion)

$$\begin{aligned} k_{t} &=\frac{84.3 \times 200 \times 10^{3}}{30 \times 10^{-3}}=562 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ &=562 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

$k_{d}=\frac{A_{d} E}{L_{d}}$ (Stiffness in unthreaded region)

$A_{d}$( major diameter c/s area )

$=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{d}^{2}=0.785 \times 144$

$=113.04 \mathrm{mm}^{2}$

$L_{d}$ (length of unthreaded portion) = 8mm

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad & k_{d}=\frac{113.04 \times 200 \times 10^{3}}{8 \times 10^{-3}} \\ &=2826 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}=2826 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{1}{k} &=\frac{1}{k_{t}}+\frac{1}{k_{d}} \Rightarrow k=\frac{k_{d} k_{t}}{k_{d}+k_{t}}=\frac{2826 \times 562}{2826+562} \\ &=468.77 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **465** (acceptable range: [460, 470]).

pp:me:2014:q36-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 36
pp:me:2014:q36-s4.question: A frame is subjected to a load P as shown in the figure. The frame has a constant flexural rigidity EI. The effect of axial load is neglected. The deflection at point A due to the applied load P is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: Bending moment in section AB $$\begin{aligned} M &=-P x \\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P} &=-x \end{aligned}$$ Bending moment in section BC: $$\begin{aligned} M&=-P L\\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P}&=-L \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{1}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L}(-P x)(-x) d x+\int_{0}^{L}(-P L)(-L) d x\right] \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{P}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L} x^{2} d x+L^{2} \int_{0}^{L} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{P}{E I}\left(\frac{L^{3}}{3}+L^{3}\right)=\frac{4 P L^{3}}{3 E I} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:me:2014:q37-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 37
pp:me:2014:q37-s4.question: A wardrobe (mass 100 kg, height 4 m, width 2 m, depth 1 m), symmetric about the Y-Y axis, stands on a rough level floor as shown in the figure. A force P is applied at mid-height on the wardrobe so as to tip it about point Q without slipping. What are the minimum values of the force (in newton) and the static coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the floor and the wardrobe, respectively?

detailed_solution.markdown: We can solve this question by moment or by force triangle as this is condition of equilibrium (just to topple) $$\begin{aligned} \sum M_{Q} &=0 \\ P \times 2-m g \times 1 &=0 \\ P &=\frac{m g}{2}=\frac{981}{2} \\ &=490.5 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$ as P is horizontal force and it will be over come by friction force $P=\left(f_{s}\right)_{\max }$[ as this is at verge of motion ] $$\begin{aligned} 490.5 &=\mu_{s} m g \\ \mu_{s} &=0.5 \end{aligned}$$ OR $$\begin{aligned} \tan \theta &=\frac{2}{1} \\ \theta &=63.4349^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$ Wardrobe is about to topple about pt Q so there will be contact force from point Q on the wardrobe $$\begin{aligned} \frac{W}{P} &=\tan \theta=2 \\ P &=\frac{W}{2}=\frac{981}{2}=490.5 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$ Two components of R will balance W and P and horizontal component (parallel to contacting surface is called friction and perpendicular to contacting surface is called normal reaction) $$\begin{aligned} R \cos \theta &=\text { friction force } \\ &=P(\text { in magnitude }) \\ \left(f_{s}\right)_{\max } &=P=490.5 \\ \text{and}\qquad \left(f_{s}\right)_{\max } &=\mu_{s} m g\\ \mu_{s} m g &=490.5 \\ \mu_{s} &=0.5 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2014:q38-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 38
pp:me:2014:q38-s4.question: Torque and angular speed data over one cycle for a shaft carrying a flywheel are shown in the figures. The moment of inertia (in kg.$m^{2}$) of the flywheel is _______

$$\begin{aligned} I &=? \\ E &=3000 \times\left[\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}\right]-1500 \times[2 \pi-\pi] \\ &=3000 \times \frac{\pi}{2}-1500 \pi=0 \\ T_{\text {mean }} \times & 2 \pi=E \\ T_{\text {mean }} &=\frac{E}{2 \pi}=0 \\ \omega_{\min } &=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{at} 0=\pi / 2 \\ \omega_{\max } &=20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{at} 0=\pi \\ C_{s} &=\frac{\omega_{\max }-\omega_{\min }}{\frac{\omega_{\max }+\omega_{\min }}{2}} \\ &=\frac{2\left\{\omega_{\max }-\omega_{\min }\right\}}{\omega_{\max }+\omega_{\min }} \\ &=\frac{2 \times\{20-10\}}{20+10}=0.67 \\ \Delta E &=3000 \times \frac{\pi}{2}=1500 \pi \\ \Delta E &=I \omega^{2} C_{s}\\ 1500 \pi &=I \times \omega_{\text {mean }}^{2} \times 0.67 \\ 1500 \pi &=I \times\left\{\frac{20+10}{2}\right\}^{2} \times 0.67 \\ I &=\frac{1500 \pi}{15^{2} \times 0.67}=31.26 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q39-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 39
pp:me:2014:q39-s4.question: A single degree of freedom system has a mass of 2 kg, stiffness 8 N/m and viscous damping  ratio 0.02. The dynamic magnification factor at an excitation frequency of 1.5 rad/s is  _______

pp:me:2014:q40-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 40
pp:me:2014:q40-s4.question: A ladder AB of length 5 m and weight (W) 600 N is resting against a wall. Assuming frictionless contact at the floor (B) and the wall (A), the magnitude of the force P (in newton) required to maintain equilibrium of the ladder is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: For ladder to be in equilibrium $\Sigma F=0$ $\Sigma M=0$ (about any point 'or' line) FBD of lader $$\begin{aligned} W &=N_{B}=600 \quad \ldots(i) \\ P &=N_{A} \quad \ldots(ii)\\ \Sigma M_{A} &=0 \\ W \times 2+P \times 3 &-N_{B} \times 4=0 \\ P &=\frac{600 \times 4-600 \times 2}{3} \\ &=\frac{600 \times 2}{3}=400 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}$$ $N_{A}$ is also equal to 4 nn Therefore, the correct answer is **400** (acceptable range: [399, 401]).

pp:me:2014:q41-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 41
pp:me:2014:q41-s4.question: A closed system contains 10 kg of saturated liquid ammonia at 10$^{\circ}$C. Heat addition required to convert the entire liquid into saturated vapour at a constant pressure is 16.2 MJ. If the entropy of the saturated liquid is 0.88 kJ/kg.K, the entropy (in kJ/kg.K) of saturated vapour is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown:
For closed system, $\delta Q=T d S$

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \delta Q&=m T\left(s_{g}-s_{f}\right) \\ \therefore s_{g}&=\frac{\delta Q}{m T}+s_{f} \\ s_{g} &=\frac{16.2 \times 10^{3}}{10 \times(273+3)}+0.88 \\ &=5.724+0.88\\ &=6.604 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK}  \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **6.55** (acceptable range: [6.4, 6.7]).

pp:me:2014:q42-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 42
pp:me:2014:q42-s4.question: A plane wall has a thermal conductivity of 1.15 W/m.K.  If the inner surface is at 1100$^{\circ}$C and the outer surface is at 350$^{\circ}$C, then the design thickness (in meter) of the wall to maintain a steady heat flux of 2500 W/$m^{2}$ should be _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} k&=1.15 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} ;\; T_{1}=1100^{o};\;T_{2}=350^{o}C\\ q&=2500 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ \mathrm{T}_{1}&=1100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}_{i}, T_{2}=350^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q&=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{R_{t}} \\ \frac{Q}{A}&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ q&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ 2500&=\frac{1.15(1100-350)}{\delta} \\ \text{or}\quad \delta&=0.345 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.34** (acceptable range: [0.33, 0.35]).

pp:me:2014:q44-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 44
pp:me:2014:q44-s4.question: Consider a velocity field $\vec{V}=K(y\hat{i}+x\hat{k})$ where K is a constant. The vorticity, $\Omega_{Z}$, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Velocity vector

$$\begin{aligned} \vec{V} &=K(y \hat{i}+x \hat{k}) \\ &=K y \hat{i}+K x \hat{k} \end{aligned}$$

where,

$u=K y, v=0 \text { and } w=K x$

Vorticity about z-axis,

$$\begin{aligned} \Omega_{z} &=\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} &=0, \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=K \\ \therefore \quad \Omega_{z} &=0-K=-K \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2014:q45-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 45
pp:me:2014:q45-s4.question: Water flows through a tube of diameter 25 mm at an average velocity of 1.0 m/s. The properties of water are $\rho =1000 kg/m^{3}$ , $\mu =7.25\times 10^{-4} N.s/m^{2}$ , $k=0.625 W/m.K, P_{r}=4.85$.  Using $Nu=0.023 Re^{0.8} Pr^{0.4}$,  the convective heat transfer coefficient (in $W/m^{2}.K$ )is______

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown:
Reynolds number,

$$\begin{aligned} \operatorname{Re} &=\frac{\rho V d}{\mu}=\frac{1000 \times 1 \times 25 \times 10^{-3}}{7.25 \times 10^{-4}} \\ &=34482.75 \\ \operatorname{Pr} &=4.85 \\ \mathrm{Nu} &=0.023 \mathrm{Re}^{0.8} \mathrm{Pr} .^{0.4} \\ \mathrm{Nu} &=0.023 \times(34482.758)^{0.8}(4.85)^{0.4} \\ &=184.546 \\ \text { also, } \quad \mathrm{Nu} &=\frac{h d}{k} \\ \text { or } \quad h &=\frac{\mathrm{Nuk}}{d}=\frac{184.546 \times 0.625}{25 \times 10^{-3}}\\ &=4613.66 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2014:q46-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 46
pp:me:2014:q46-s4.question: Two identical metal blocks L and M (specific heat = 0.4 kJ/kg.K), each having a mass of 5 kg, are initially at 313 K. A reversible refrigerator extracts heat from block L and rejects heat to block M until the temperature of block L reaches 293 K. The final temperature (in K) of block M is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: Specified heat, $$\begin{aligned} c&=0.4 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \text{ each body}\\ \text{Mass:}m&=5 \mathrm{kg} \quad \text { each body } \end{aligned}$$ Initial temperature, $T_{1}=313 \mathrm{K} \quad \text { each body }$ Final temprature of block L $T_{2}=293 \mathrm{K}$ Let $\quad T_{f}=$ Final temperature of block M, Entropy change of block L $\Delta S_{L}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}$ Entropy change of block M $\Delta S_{M}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}$ Entropy change of universe, $$\begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }} &=\Delta S_{L}+\Delta S_{M} \\ &=mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}+mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}} \end{aligned}$$ For a reversible refrigeration, $$\begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }}&=0 \\ m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&+m_{c} \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}=0\\ mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}} &=e^{0}=1 \\ T_{f} &=\frac{T_{1}^{2}}{T_{2}}=\frac{(313)^{2}}{293}=334.36 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **334** (acceptable range: [333, 335]).

pp:me:2014:q47-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 47
pp:me:2014:q47-s4.question: Steam with specific enthalpy (h) 3214 kJ/kg enters an adiabatic turbine operating at steady state with a flow rate 10 kg/s. As it expands, at a point where h is 2920 kJ/kg, 1.5 kg/s is extracted for heating purposes. The remaining 8.5 kg/s further expands to the turbine exit, where h = 2374 kJ/kg. Neglecting changes in kinetic and potential energies, the net power output (in kW) of the turbine   is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} m_{1} &=10 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{2}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{3}=8.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ h_{1} &=3214 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{2}=2920 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=2374 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ W_{T} &=m_{1}\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+m_{3}\left(h_{2}-h_{3}\right) \\ &=10(3214-2920)+8.5(2920-2374) \\ &=7581 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **7581** (acceptable range: [7580, 7582]).

pp:me:2014:q48-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 48
pp:me:2014:q48-s4.question: Two infinite parallel plates are placed at a certain distance apart. An infinite radiation shield is inserted between the plates without touching any of them to reduce heat exchange between the plates. Assume that the emissivities of plates and radiation shield are equal. The ratio of the net heat exchange between the plates with and without the shield is

detailed_solution.markdown: $\epsilon_{1}=\epsilon_{s}=\epsilon_{2}=\epsilon$ $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{R}(\text { with N shields})&=(N+1)\left(\frac{2}{\epsilon}-1\right) \\ \text { R(without shield) }&=\frac{2}{\epsilon}-1 \\ \left(\frac{Q}{A}\right)_{\text {with } N \text { shield }}&=\frac{1}{N+1}\left(\frac{Q}{A}\right)_{\text {without shild }} \\ \therefore \frac{Q_{\text {with shield }}}{Q_{\text {without shield }}}=\frac{1}{N+1}&=\frac{1}{2} \quad(\because N=1) \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2014:q49-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 49
pp:me:2014:q49-s4.question: In a compression ignition engine, the inlet air pressure is 1 bar and the pressure at the end of isentropic compression is 32.42 bar. The expansion ratio is 8. Assuming ratio of specific heats ($\gamma$ ) as 1.4, the air standard efficiency (in percent) is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: Given, $p_{1}=1$ bar, $p_{2}=32.42$ bar $$\begin{aligned} \gamma &=\frac{C_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.4 \\ \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}} &=\frac{V_{1}}{V_{3}}=8 \end{aligned}$$ For process 1-2 $$\begin{aligned} p_{1} v_{1}^{\gamma}&=p_{2} v_{2}^{\gamma} \\ \therefore\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}&=\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=32.42 \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}} &=(32.42)^{1 / 1.4}=11.999 \approx 12 \\ r_{c} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=\frac{V_{1}}{8} \times \frac{12}{V_{1}}=1.5 \\ \eta_{\text {Diesel }} &=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{C}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{C}-1\right)}\right] \\ &=1-\frac{1}{12^{0.4}}\left[\frac{1.5^{1.4}-1}{1.4 \times 0.5}\right] \\ &=0.596=59.6 \% \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **60** (acceptable range: [59, 61]).

pp:me:2014:q53-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 53
pp:me:2014:q53-s4.question: A cylindrical riser of 6 cm diameter and 6 cm height has to be designed for a sand casting mould for producing a steel rectangular plate casting of 7 cm x 10 cm x 2 cm dimensions having the total solidification time of 1.36 minute. The total solidification time (in minute) of the riser is  _______

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} V_{\text {casting }}&=7 \times 10 \times 2=140 \mathrm{cm}^{3} \\ A_{\text {casting }}&= 2(7 \times 10+7 \times 2+2 \times 10) \\ &=2 \times(70 \times 20 \times 14)\\&=2 \times 104=208 \mathrm{cm}^{2}\\ \qquad\left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {casting }}&=\frac{140}{208}=0.673 \mathrm{cm} \\ \qquad\left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {Top Riser }}&=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{3}}{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{2}+\pi d^{2}}=\frac{d}{5}\\ &=1.2\mathrm{cm}\qquad(\therefore d=h=6\mathrm{cm}) \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {Bottom Riser }}&=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{3}}{\frac{\pi}{2} d^{2}+\pi d^{2}}=\frac{d}{6}=1 \mathrm{cm} \\ \frac{t_{R}}{t_{C}}&= \frac{(V / A)_{\text {Top Riser }}^{2}}{(V / A)_{\text {Casting }}^{2}}=\left(\frac{1.2}{0.673}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow t_{R}&=4.133 \text { minute } \text { (for top riser) }\\ \frac{t_{R}}{t_{C}} &=\frac{(V / A)_{\text {Bottom Riser }}^{2}}{(V / A)_{\text {Casting }}^{2}}=\left(\frac{1}{0.673}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow t_{R} &=3 \text { minute } \quad \text { (for bottom riser) } \end{aligned}$$

Solidification time considering top and bottom riser comes under range given in the answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3.5** (acceptable range: [2.5, 4.5]).

pp:me:2014:q54-s4.title: GATE ME 2014 | Set 4 | Question: 54
pp:me:2014:q54-s4.question: A cast iron block of 200 mm length is being shaped in a shaping machine with a depth of cut of  4 mm, feed of 0.25 mm/stroke and the tool principal cutting edge angle of 30$^{\circ}$. Number of cutting strokes per minute is 60. Using specific energy for cutting as 1.49 J/$mm^{3}$, the average power consumption (in watt) is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
The volume rate of material removal is:

$$\begin{aligned} Q&=f d L N \\ \text { where } f(\text { feed })&=0.25 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{stroke} \\ d(\text { depth of } \mathrm{cut})&=4 \mathrm{mm} \\ \quad L(\text { length of block })&=200 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$
